title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v26
author: Daniel Park
description: Motivation: bring profiling baselines and representative workload runners up-to-date for the next round of performance regressions and model-variant comparisons. This PR bundles: 1) new profiling baselines for quantized 4-bit and 8-bit model variants, 2) updated representative workload runners that exercise streaming, KV cache reuse, and long-context batching, and 3) a lightweight reporting pipeline that aggregates profiling artifacts into the benchmark-lab dashboard.
commits: Initial baseline artifacts and runner scaffolding (add profiling/benchmarks/*)
Add quantized baseline configs (4q, 8q) and sample inputs for deterministic runs
Introduce reporting pipeline tasks (dag + uploader) and S3 layout changes
Fix: runner parallelism control and stable RNG seeds for reproducible profiles
Docs: update benchmark-lab README with runbook and interpretation guide
Tests: add CI job to run a smoke profiling run and validate artifact schema
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Please add deterministic RNG seeding for the long-context tests so CI runs are reproducible.
Daniel Park (author): Added deterministic seeding and updated the smoke test to assert identical hashes for artifact metadata between runs.
Marco Li: Can we reduce the default parallelism on the representative runner? It saturates our small CI GPU workers. Requested to expose config with sane defaults.
Daniel Park (author): Exposed 'max_workers' config with default 2 in runners and added a note to the README.
Sofia Nguyen: CI pipeline looks good but the uploader should tolerate transient S3 5xxs; please add retry logic.
Daniel Park (author): Implemented exponential backoff retry in uploader and added unit test for retry path.
merge_commit_message: Add profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v26\n\nIncludes quantized baselines (4q/8q), representative runners exercising streaming and KV cache reuse, and a reporting DAG that uploads profiling artifacts to S3 and updates the benchmark dashboard. Improved runner determinism and CI smoke coverage.
release_notes:
- Added profiling baselines for 4-bit and 8-bit quantized variants
- Representative workload runners updated for streaming, KV cache reuse, and long-context batching
- New reporting pipeline to ingest profiling artifacts into benchmark-lab dashboard
- CI smoke job to validate profiling artifact schema and reproducibility
notes_on_testing: Unit tests added for uploader retry, smoke profiling run added to CI pipeline, manual verification performed on staging benchmark cluster (bench-qa). Reproduced baseline artifacts twice to confirm stable metrics.
motivation_and_context: Recent regressions reported in ENG-2148 highlighted variability between quantized model variants and the hosted runtime artifact layout. This work standardizes baseline generation and adds a lightweight reporting path so the bench team can quickly detect regressions in perf and memory metrics.
how_to_run_locally: See benchmark-lab/README.md and the profiling baselines README for example commands. Typical run: ./scripts/benchlab/collect_baseline.sh --profile quantized_4bit --output ./artifacts && python benchmark-lab/reporting/uploader.py --artifact ./artifacts/metadata.json
observability_and_metric_changes: Reporting pipeline emits benchmark_lab.profile.run and benchmark_lab.profile.upload metrics; added tags for model_variant and quantization_profile. Dashboard updated to surface median and p95 token latency and peak GPU memory by profile.
follow_up_tasks: - ENG-2210: Add automated regression alerts when median token latency deviates >8% from baseline\n- Integrate baseline artifacts with canary runs in perf-canary repo\n- Extend runners to support multi-GPU sharded profiles
ci_check_details: CI: profiling-smoke (pass), unit (pass), lint (pass), e2e (skipped: heavy), reporting-integration (pass). A transient S3 test failed on first run and was retried; final status green.
risk_and_rollout: Low risk: changes are mostly additive and behind configs. Reporting DAG can be toggled via feature-flag. Runners default to conservative parallelism to avoid CI/GPU saturation.
